category_note: Custom classification — no listed category (kinetic-type, stat, charts, logo-reveal, lower-thirds, maps, webpage, news, tweet, asset-fusion) cleanly fits. This is asset-free geometric shapes (a 6-cell bento grid, no text, no data, no logo asset, no map, no captured source) resolving via one animated instrument (a diagonal ruler line). Closest in spirit is logo-reveal (a brand identity assembling into one coherent state) but it fails structurally: logo-reveal requires a user-supplied logo asset and a literal draw-on/mask-reveal of that logo, whereas this shot has no logo asset at all — the 'identity' being revealed is a token/grid system, not a mark. 'diagram' (flowchart block: nodes/edges/labels) was also considered and rejected — this shot has no connectors, nodes, or labels, only rectangles + one line. Treated as a form category (`asset_needs: []`, user/brief supplies all content) and a hand-authored gap per director.md's reuse-first heuristic — no catalog block covers 'bento cells resolve in sequence as a line sweeps the diagonal,' so `block` is intentionally omitted (Builder hand-authors).
style: Architectural, restrained, monochrome. A drafting instrument (hairline ruler with tick terminators) sweeps the frame's diagonal once and a misaligned 6-cell bento grid resolves into one governed, running system — then is quietly rebuilt for the next pass. Reads as architecture settling, not a UI micro-interaction or a sci-fi scan: zero glow, zero spring, zero bounce, zero overshoot anywhere. No hue — six neutrals only. No text, no cursor, no code iconography.
font_note: No text anywhere in this composition per brief — font is not applicable.
beats_note: Pass-boundary accents in seconds: build-pass start, running-hold (peak) start, settle-pass start, tail static-hold start, loop end. Per-cell resolve/revert timing lives in content.timing (transcribed verbatim from the brief).
build_note: Hand-authored — no catalog block matches this motif (see category_note). Builder implements directly against content below plus the brief's hand-off note (single paused GSAP timeline on window.__timelines, tl.seek(0) after build, fromTo tweens only — no bare tl.set() for the loop reset, deterministic only, square corners baked into root since mp4 has no alpha, run `npm run check` before rendering).

ground.note: Nothing else enters the frame. Exactly 6 cells + 1 line, nothing more — no text, no cursor, no code brackets, no literal Figma iconography.

grid_geometry.layout: 3 cols x 3 rows within the content box

resolved_state.note: Identical rule for all 6 cells — 'running' state.
resolved_state.corner_radius: 4px, constant — radius never animates in either state, so the story stays about alignment, weight, and fill only

static_state_per_cell.note: Hand-set, never random, small enough to read as deliberate misalignment rather than a rendering glitch. Nothing rotates or skews — every edge stays axis-true.

instrument.form: one diagonal straightedge line — a hairline rule with a short perpendicular tick at each end, like a drafting tool's dimension-line terminator
instrument.path: content box's top-left corner to bottom-right corner, extending slightly past each corner so it visibly enters and exits off-canvas
instrument.behavior: the only element that moves independently; everything else changes only because the line passed over it
instrument.must_read_as: a ruler being drawn across a drawing, not a sci-fi scan

choreography.name: At rest (loop bookends)
choreography.description: Grid sits in the static_state_per_cell table above, completely still — nothing tweens, nothing breathes. Line is fully off-canvas, invisible. This exact frame opens and closes the loop.

choreography.name: Build pass
choreography.description: The line enters off-canvas at the content box's top-left corner and travels the box diagonal to its bottom-right corner, extending slightly past each corner. As it crosses each cell's position, that cell resolves from static to resolved (position snaps, stroke unifies and darkens, fill fades in) in a single local tween — no bounce, no overshoot. Cells resolve in order A -> B -> D -> C -> E -> F, each local resolve ~0.35s with slight overlap (~0.1-0.15s) into the next, reading as one continuous wave rather than six clicks.

choreography.name: Hold — the peak
choreography.description: Line has exited off-canvas bottom-right, invisible. Grid sits fully resolved: aligned, unified stroke, filled. This is the longest beat and the one most likely to be the frame someone actually sees — nothing moves.

choreography.name: Settle pass
choreography.description: The line re-enters at the same top-left corner and travels the same diagonal, same direction — never reversed. As it crosses each cell, that cell reverts from resolved back to static, in the SAME order it resolved (A -> B -> D -> C -> E -> F), not the reverse order. This is what makes it read as the system being rebuilt for the next pass rather than a rewind.

choreography.name: Return to rest
choreography.description: Line exits off-canvas bottom-right, invisible. Grid is back in the exact static_state_per_cell table state — pixel-identical to step 1. Hold briefly, then loop.

build_pass_per_cell_windows.note: Approximate, overlapping ~0.1-0.15s into the next so the wave reads as continuous.

settle_pass_per_cell.note: Mirrors the build-pass order (A first, F last) scaled proportionally into the 1.8s settle window (3.8-5.6s), each local revert ~0.30s. Brief gives this as proportional/approximate, not exact absolute windows — do not invent precision beyond what's specified here.

easing.applies_to: every tween — the line's travel and every per-cell local resolve/revert
easing.character: architecture settling, not a UI micro-interaction

loop_rule.statement: t=6.000 must be pixel-identical to t=0.000 — same transforms, same stroke weights, same fill, line fully off-canvas and invisible at both ends.

implementation_notes: Rebuild, not an edit — supersedes the prior kinetic-type 'MODERN' attempt entirely; start fresh from this grid+line concept.
Square corners baked into the composition root (site rounds the tile in CSS); mp4 has no alpha so any baked rounding would render as black wedges.
Single paused GSAP timeline registered on window.__timelines; tl.seek(0) after build.

Only fromTo tweens on interpolable properties (x, y, opacity, scale, stroke-width or border-width, background-color/fill, clip-path). No bare tl.set() for the loop reset — build the tail state as real fromTo tweens (or a duplicated/never-animated layer trick) so backward seeks render correctly.
Deterministic only — no Date.now(), no Math.random(), no physics. All six per-cell static offsets and stroke weights are hard-coded from static_state_per_cell, not generated.
Run `npm run check` inside videos/visual-identity-motion/ (lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast) before rendering.
